title: Heavy Applause
blurb: A full room going at it, hundreds of pairs of hands rather than a polite dozen. Crowd applause sounds simple and is genuinely awkward to fake, because real clapping never lands in sync and the tail decays unevenly as people give up at different moments. This recording has that raggedness. Use it sincerely at the end of a presentation clip, or witheringly in a voice call after somebody states the obvious at length. Slow it right down and you get a slow clap — a related tool with considerably worse manners.
origin: A generic recording of a large audience applauding.
